dialogue.text: The first morning of the new school term -- and Aoi is already running late.
No, no, no -- not on the very first day!
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: anxious

dialogue.text: Aoi skids to a stop at the corner, one hand on her school bag, breath catching in the cold morning air.
She had left home on time.
But halfway to school, she remembered the attendance form she forgot on the kitchen table.
She ran back for it. Then ran again. And now the pedestrian light is red.
I had it this morning... I know I did...
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: anxious

dialogue.text: Beside the crosswalk, a little girl in a yellow hat stands alone, shoulders shaking.
Um...
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: anxious

dialogue.text: Are you okay?
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: anxious

dialogue.text: Hic... my brother went away...
dialogue.speaker: Little Girl

dialogue.text: The girl clutches a rabbit keychain so tightly her fingers have gone white.
You got separated?
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: neutral

dialogue.text: He said stay here... but he didn't come back...
dialogue.speaker: Little Girl

dialogue.text: The walk signal changes. Students stream past them toward school.
Aoi glances at the road. Then at the girl.
...I can't just leave you.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: determined

dialogue.text: Do you know your brother's name?
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: anxious

dialogue.text: Haru.
dialogue.speaker: Little Girl

dialogue.text: Okay. Let's stand by the police box.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: determined

dialogue.text: It's only a short distance away, but the girl's steps are tiny and uneven.
At the neighborhood koban, the officer kneels to the girl's height and speaks gently into a radio.
You did the right thing bringing her here.
dialogue.speaker: Officer

dialogue.text: I just... happened to see her.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: embarrassed

dialogue.text: She says it quietly, but her pulse is still pounding.
A minute later, footsteps slap against the pavement outside.
Haru!
dialogue.speaker: Little Girl

dialogue.text: A middle-school boy bursts in, pale and breathless, and the girl runs straight into him.
You can't leave your sister alone like that.
dialogue.speaker: Officer

dialogue.text: I thought you went away forever...
dialogue.speaker: Little Girl

dialogue.text: She's been scared for a while.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: sad

dialogue.text: I know. I'm sorry. I only went to ask for directions...
dialogue.speaker: Haru

dialogue.text: His voice cracks on the last word.
Aoi looks away, giving them a little privacy.
It's okay now.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: smile

dialogue.text: Thank you, big sister.
dialogue.speaker: Little Girl

dialogue.text: ...You're welcome.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: smile

dialogue.text: The girl smiles through drying tears. Small, uneven, but real.
When Aoi finally steps back outside, the town has fully woken up.
And the clock on the station sign makes her stomach drop.
Ah...
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: anxious

dialogue.text: First period is definitely starting.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: anxious

dialogue.text: For one weak second, she imagines turning around and going home.
Her shoes feel heavy. Her face burns just thinking about opening the classroom door late.
They're all going to look at me...
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: embarrassed

dialogue.text: She presses the attendance form against her chest.
Then she remembers the little girl reaching for her brother.
But... I did the right thing.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: determined

dialogue.text: The words are barely above a whisper.
Still, hearing them makes her straighten a little.
So... I'll go.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi
dialogue.label: determined

dialogue.text: Aoi takes one slow breath, then starts running again -- late, flustered, and somehow just a little less afraid of the day waiting for her.
